- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 76+), overshooting by 3–5% in 3–5 day horizon; apply dampening factor of 0.95–0.97 to peak forecasts.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize continuation; add 0.5–1% downward bias to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses early correction phases; apply 1–2% downward adjustment if true outcome shows early dip after peak.
